children: 2004 ET - Crypto remains under pressure Monday, with Bitcoin down 0.2% at $64,821 after breaking below another key level at $65,000 over the weekend. Ethereum sinks deeper past the $2,000 mark to trade at $1,811--its lowest level since early July. Bitcoin's renewed collapse reflects compounding bearish factors, from weak sentiment in financial markets to growing pessimism about inflation and tight monetary policy, says Samer Hasn at XS.com. That's prompting investors to exit Bitcoin exchange-traded funds at an accelerating pace, and creating more risk of miners and treasury companies liquidating holdings, the analyst says. This week's economic data, Fed minutes and a speech from Fed Chair Warsh are in focus. Any signals that reinforce hawkish expectations could weigh on crypto. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)

1936 ET - Asian currencies consolidate against the dollar, but may be weighed by risk-off sentiment. These currencies could "remain on the defensive at the start of the week as elevated U.S. Treasury yields and renewed weakness in technology shares weigh on sentiment," OCBC Group Research strategists say in a note. "For the week ahead, we would watch whether foreign equity selling in Korea and Taiwan eases, alongside developments in oil prices, technology shares and U.S. Treasury yields," the strategists add. The U.S. dollar edges 0.1% lower to 1,333.90 won and is flat at 1.2879 Singapore dollars, while the Australian dollar is steady at US$0.6772, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

1930 ET - Japan's economic performance in the third quarter probably won't prevent the BOJ from raising rates in December, says Capital Economics' Marcel Thieliant. Indeed, it seems increasingly likely that the BOJ will have to tighten policy more aggressively than expected as inflation is about to surge. While the GDP print was rather discouraging it was hardly a disaster, the economist says. Growth is set to overshoot the BOJ's median forecast of a 0.7% on quarter rise across the fiscal year started in April even if output remains stagnant over the next couple of quarters, CE says. Plus, the BOJ tankan survey indicates the most favorable business conditions since the early-1990s. Accordingly, CE still expects a rate hike in December. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)

1929 ET - Reserve Bank of Australia Governor Michele Bullock will speak at a forum held by the country's corporate regulator on Tuesday, and financial markets will again be hanging on her every word. There's a sense that the RBA is done raising interest rates, and this would be an opportunity for her to cement those ideas. Still, she's likely to want to leave the door open for a hike in either December of February. Inflation remains elevated and the investment story is supporting growth. It's probable that the bank is sidelined for now. But any nasty rise in coming CPI data will quickly bring the RBA back into play. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)

1916 ET - JGB futures fall in the early Tokyo session, tracking Friday's price declines in U.S. Treasurys market. Both JGBs and Treasurys tend to move in tandem. JGB prices may also be weighed by prospects of further BOJ rate increases. The BOJ will likely "tighten further despite sluggish GDP growth," Capital Economics' Marcel Thieliant says, noting preliminary government data released earlier showing Japan's economy contracted in 3Q. "It looks increasingly likely that the Bank will have to tighten policy more aggressively than we've been anticipating as inflation is about to surge," the head of Asia-Pacific adds. Benchmark 10-year JGB futures are 0.16 yen lower at 126.17 yen. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

1913 ET - The dollar is expected to rise further to 162 yen in 2027, five members of Morgan Stanley's research team say in a note. On the one hand, there's yen-negative impact of global risk appetite, terms of trade and investor demand for carry, the members say. On other hand, there's yen-positive factor of tighter U.S.-Japan rate spreads. The former is likely to have a larger effect, partly because markets will probably continue to see the Bank of Japan as "behind the curve," limiting yen-positive impact of higher Japanese rates, the members add. Morgan Stanley's 4Q 2027 target for dollar-yen is 162. The dollar is 0.1% higher at Y159.77, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

1850 ET - Japanese stocks may trade rangebound as uncertainty over the Federal Reserve's further rate increases continues. Drops in U.S. technology stocks on Friday could weigh on the market. Nikkei futures are up 0.1% at 61320 on the SGX. The dollar is at 159.80 yen, compared with Y160.10 as of Friday's Tokyo stock market close. Investors remain focused on domestic earnings and crude oil prices. Dentsu Group is scheduled to report its quarterly results later Monday. The Nikkei Stock Average rose 0.5% to 61142.35 on Friday. (kosaku.narioka@wsj.com)
